findings.title: Array-valued iss claim bypasses allowedIss allowlist via loose any-match
findings.evidence: validateClaimValues() accepts a claim when ANY element matches: line 159 `if (!values.some(v => allowed.some(a => a.test(v))))` only throws if no element matches. verifyToken() (lines 209-227) derives `values = arrayValue ? value : [value]` from the attacker-controlled payload and routes every non-date validator, including the `iss` validator registered at lines 474-476, into this loose matcher at line 226. RFC 7519 section 4.1.1 defines `iss` as a single StringOrURI, and upstream fixed exactly this in 5.0.6 (CVE-2025-30144 / GHSA-gm45-q3v2-6cf8) by making non-array-enabled validators require `values.every(...)`. Reachability: an attacker who can present a JWT whose signature verifies against a key the verifier trusts (e.g. a shared HMAC secret) sets `iss` to `["https://attacker.example", "https://trusted.example"]`; the trusted element satisfies the bound exactStringClaimMatcher (lines 13-15, 39-53), `allowedIss` passes, and the verifier returns success while the token actually names an untrusted issuer, i.e. authentication bypass by spoofing. The same loose any-match is used for jti, sub and nonce (lines 466-484).

findings.title: JSON-array JWT payload silently skips every claim validator
findings.evidence: decode() validates the payload with `if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object')` (line 38); because `typeof [] === 'object'`, a JWT whose payload segment decodes to a JSON array is accepted. In verifyToken() each configured validator is gated on `if (!(claim in payload)) continue` (line 216) and requiredClaims uses the same membership test (line 200), and `'iss' in []` is false, so iss/aud/sub/jti/nonce/exp/nbf validation is silently skipped while the signature is still checked (line 139). Upstream fixed this in 6.3.0 (CVE-2026-107723) by adding `Array.isArray(payload)`; the array header case is already rejected, showing the omission is a bug, not intended behavior. Reachability: an attacker able to obtain a token signed by a key the verifier trusts (shared secret / same signing service) submits an array payload such as `["attacker","role:admin"]` to bypass the allowedIss/allowedAud/expiry guarantees.
